# Intakes — what Métis reads

*Generated from `connectors/intakes.json`.*

Everything Métis reads. **No access mode runs anything** (X-7a): a database read for its structure is an intake source, and the same database reached to check a test's outcome is the System Under Test. Only the first is available, and that is structural — `executes_against_sut` is a schema `const` of `false`.

| intake | status | access | command | reader |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ac-mined | working | `authored_file` | `metis ac-mine` | `metis_mcp.model_sources.ac_mining` |
| authored | working | `authored_file` | `metis land` | `metis_mcp.model_sources.sources` |
| code | working | `local_files` | `metis land` | `metis_mcp.model_sources.sources, code_analysis.packs.jvm-structural, code_analysis.packs.jvm-behaviour` |
| database | partial | `read_only_connection` | `metis data catalogue` | `code_analysis.db_catalogue` |
| jira | partial | `read_only_connection` | `metis intake fetch` | `code_analysis.tracker` |
| knowledge | working | `authored_file` | `metis knowledge check` | `metis_mcp.model_sources.knowledge, metis_mcp.model_sources.glossary` |
| openapi | working | `local_files` | `metis land` | `code_analysis.openapi` |
| spec-kit | working | `local_files` | `metis spec` | `metis_mcp.model_sources.spec_kit` |
| structure | working | `authored_file` | `metis structure check` | `metis_mcp.model_sources.structure` |

### What in the source produces what

`lands` names the labels; this names the thing in the source that produces each. Absent where the shape is not unambiguous — an invented shape is worse than none.

**code**

- Spring @RestController / @RequestMapping method → `Endpoint`
- a return or throw that constructs a response → `DeclaredOutcome`
- a branch that selects one outcome over its sibling → `Check`
- a @ControllerAdvice @ExceptionHandler method → `ExceptionMapping`
- a handler parameter → `Parameter`
- a DTO or record reachable from a payload → `Class`

**database**

- a row of information_schema.tables → `Table`
- a row of information_schema.views → `View`
- a row of information_schema.columns → `Column`
- a schema in the catalogue → `Schema`
- the connection's database → `Database`

**jira**

- a Jira issue's summary or description, where EARS-conformant → `Requirement`
- a Jira issue whose text is free prose → `Finding`
- the issue itself → `JiraItem`
- one fetch → `Episode`

**openapi**

- an operation object → `Endpoint`
- a response object → `DeclaredOutcome`
- a parameter object → `Parameter`
- a component schema → `Class`

**structure**

- a page entry in structure.json → `Page`
- an element entry, at any depth → `UiElement`

**uif**

- metadata.title or metadata.description, if EARS-conformant → `Requirement`
- the document itself → `Episode`
- free prose that is not EARS-conformant → `Finding`

**zephyr**

- a Zephyr Scale case's objective or name, where EARS-conformant → `Requirement`
- a case whose text is free prose → `Finding`
- the test case itself → `ZephyrItem`
- one fetch → `Episode`

### When a fact is dated from

Every `Episode` requires `t_recorded`. This says where it comes from, and how it misleads — an intake whose answer is "extraction time" says so rather than implying a real timestamp.

| intake | anchored on | pitfall |
|---|---|---|
| code | the commit the CPG was built from — `anchor_commit` on every recovered node | rebased or squashed history loses individual commit dates, so a fact's age is the age of the squash and not of the change. v1 preferred PR merge time for this reason; nothing here reads PR metadata |
| database | extraction time — `datetime.now()`, because a catalogue carries no timestamp of its own | a catalogue read is undated by nature: the answer describes the database as it was at read time and cannot say when it last changed |
| jira | the time the UIF was generated — `scope.uif_generated_at`, stamped at fetch | that is when METIS read the tracker, not when the item last changed. The tracker's own updated-at is not read, so a stale ticket and a fresh one are indistinguishable here |
| openapi | the document's own version field where it has one; otherwise the file's mtime | a contract regenerated by a build has today's mtime and last year's content |
| uif | scope.uif_generated_at, set by the extractor that produced the document | deliberately EXCLUDED from `episode_id_for`, because it changes on every extraction run and would mint a new Episode for an unchanged artefact |
| zephyr | the time the UIF was generated — `scope.uif_generated_at`, stamped at fetch | that is when METIS read the tracker, not when the item last changed. The tracker's own updated-at is not read, so a stale ticket and a fresh one are indistinguishable here |

### Reading a status

| | |
|---|---|
| `working` | a reader exists and a test exercises it |
| `partial` | a reader exists and something material is missing, named below |
| `declared` | **no reader.** The capability does not exist |

## Limits

### code
- javasrc2cpg ignores test directories by name, so test sources need a CPG rooted inside the test tree (engine.test_roots)
- an inert accessor and generated boilerplate are dropped before anything downstream reads them (X-5a)
- a type no payload chain reaches is not landed (X-6d)
- a repository's entity->table mapping is often NOT in the source — measured on a real service, @Entity/@Table/@Column were in zero files. The code proposes a table from Spring's naming strategy and the database intake confirms or refutes it (X-19)

### database
- the FIXTURE path is what the test suite exercises; the live connection is opt-in because a driver is an optional extra and the suite must keep running with none installed
- catalogue only — schemas, tables, views, columns, types, nullability, keys. It reads NO row data, and `assert_no_row_reads` checks that on every statement rather than trusting it (X-7a)
- the connection is the caller's: a credential is named by the profile as an environment variable and never reaches an argument (PLT-005)

### jira
- the FIXTURE path is what the test suite exercises; the live read is opt-in and goes through a transport the caller opens, so no HTTP library is a dependency and the suite runs with none installed
- named items only — it reads the keys it is given and does NOT crawl a project, run JQL, or follow links. A crawl is a different capability and would need arguing for
- GET only, against a closed allowlist in `tracker.ENDPOINTS`, checked by `assert_read_only` before any request is issued (X-7a)
- a Requirement is created only from EARS-conformant text. Whichever of summary/description conforms is used; free prose lands as a Finding pointing at knowledge-capture instead (S-13)
- a ticket's CLAIMED acceptance criteria are not emitted and would not be trusted if they were — mining them is `ac_mining`'s job, with its own provenance
- Atlassian Document Format descriptions are flattened to their text nodes. No bullet, heading or table structure is reconstructed, because a rendering that resembled the ticket without being it is worse than plain text

### openapi
- operations are keyed on operationId, which is a different id space from the code intake's handler signature — the two do not merge into one node today

### spec-kit
- a criterion written from the code it checks lands as `code_derived`, the weakest provenance — it can report coverage and never correctness (§4.1)
- a block with no Given/When/Then is returned marked as not-a-transition rather than forced into a shape it does not have

### structure
- authored because no pack identifies a component TYPE — none can tell a library <DataGrid> from a hand-rolled <div role="table">, and all three are a table to a person writing a test
- it does NOT carry selectors. How to find an element comes from the code that looks it up; this file says what is on the page

### test-inventory
- it lands NOTHING. The inventory feeds generation rather than the graph: `test_levels.from_pack` grades each transition by what an existing test already covers, so generation is additive (REQ-METIS-PG-01). An empty `lands` is the honest entry, not an omission
- JVM only — `javasrc2cpg` and JUnit's `@Test`. The v1 connector this replaces covered JUnit/TestNG/pytest/Playwright; nothing here reads the other three
- javasrc2cpg ignores test directories by name, so the CPG must be rooted INSIDE the test sources — a repo-rooted extraction recovers no tests and reports none, which reads identically to a project with no tests
- covering an endpoint is not covering a transition: a test that calls `GET /{id}` and asserts 200 is evidence for the 200 transition and says nothing about the 204 one. Grades are per transition for that reason

### uif
- a Requirement is created only from EARS-conformant text. Free prose — most Jira titles — lands as a Finding pointing at knowledge-capture, because `ears_pattern` has no empty form and guessing one is what ac_mining refuses to do (S-13)
- a UIF's CLAIMED acceptance criteria are never trusted into AcceptanceCriterion nodes
- the extractors that PRODUCE a UIF are not part of Métis. Métis reads the document; something else fetched it

### web
- a JSX handler binding is not structurally recoverable — jssrc2cpg keeps JSX as raw text — so react-ui recovers routes, API call sites and status setters, and no selectors
- a selector is recovered only where the code names it with a literal lookup. An element reached by walking the DOM is reported unresolved, never matched on its text
- an interpolated path is reported rather than resolved to its first fragment

### zephyr
- the FIXTURE path is what the test suite exercises; the live read is opt-in
- named test cases only — no folder walk, no cycle enumeration
- GET only, against a closed allowlist in `tracker.ENDPOINTS` (X-7a)
- `source_system` is `scale`, not `zephyr` — that is the value `intake_landing.ANCHORS` keys `ZephyrItem` on, and renaming it would detach every item from its anchor
- test STEPS are not read. Only the case's name and objective are, so what lands is what the case CLAIMS to verify and never a script — Métis generates human-executable cases and does not ingest them
- no execution result is read. A case's last run status is outcome data and Métis reports coverage, never correctness (C-11)
